posts.author: Grey
posts.content_md:
Hi all,

I finally got my D&S laser put together, but I think I got some heat sink compound (or something) on the diode lense (not the casing lense). I'm getting some patterns in the uncollimated beam. Can I just clean this with a cotton swab and some alcohol? Or will this scratch it? Suggestions?

posts.author: dave battin
posts.content_md: yes, alch should be fine ,becareful to not get it to wet as the window is cemented in place and you coud risk it decementing it if it gets to moist.

posts.author: Colin Kaminski
posts.content_md: I can never get the cotton fibers off. I use a sliver cut from a cosmetics sponge. Ask your girlfriend what one is.

posts.author: jmcclean
posts.content_md: Hi y'all, I just put together my D&S laser and also noticed the beam is dirty. So I wired up another fresh diode and also noticed some diffraction pattern in the raw beam. I think this may be knife edge diffraction around the photo diode. I am not comfortable using this beam as is and hope I have some luck using a spatial filter, otherwise it's back to the HeNe. I am having a hard time cleaning the square beam with my spatial filter though. Anyone else have similar issues using a diode with a spatial filter? Cheers, James

posts.author: dave battin
posts.content_md:
my 35mw diode had the top of the can removed to eliminate unwanted reflections from the window and the beam is/was as clean as if it went thru a spatial filter.............

![Image](http://www.geocities.com/greenpagoda/diode2.jpg)

posts.author: Jim McPherson
posts.content_md:
Be careful removing the case on diodes. Some diodes have special windows for reflection back to the photodiode. I addition some high power diodes have a gas mixture inside to preserve the operation of the diode. Taking the can off can ruin that.

-Jim

posts.author: Colin Kaminski
posts.content_md: I use a pin hole specified for the wide diameter of the beam and have had good but not perfect results with a spatial filter. If you shrink the pinhole you can get a perfectly clean beam but you use up some light. I now use cylindrical lenses to circularize the beam but if I was buying new equipment I would use anamorphic prisms.

posts.author: tpark
posts.content_md:
The diodes I've got have all had clean output, so I've been lucky. When not in use, I keep stuff covered so it doesn't get dusty. I may purchase an electrostatic filter for the house. I've made holograms with less than perfect beams (hene, no spatial filter) and you get results, but they aren't as good as when you've got a perfectly clean beam.

As far as cleaning goes, I managed to get the window of a laser pointer diode clean with some soapy water, then isopropyl alcohol. I used "dawn" dish soap, then a distilled water rinse, then the alcohol. It wasn't absolutely perfect, but I use the thing for viewing holograms only, so I didn't care that much.

--Ted.
